oakley.join: An expedition! Splendid. I've brought a notebook, two pencils and a spare pencil for emergencies. Lead on, {name}.
cheer: Splendid! Absolutely splendid! I'm minuting that in capitals.
Six years on the Committee for Knots, and it finally paid off!
Motion to declare that a triumph. Seconded. Carried. Splendid!
Did everyone see that? I'll need a witness for the minutes. Oh, I'm the witness. Splendid.
oops: Not to worry. I'll record that as 'a learning experience'. Most of my minutes are.
Hm. Let's refer that to a subcommittee and try again.
History is full of second attempts. I've read most of them. Twice.
I'm fairly sure that was my fault somehow. It usually is. I've checked the records.
oakley.win: A splendid day! I'll write it up tonight, every word. Possibly in two volumes.

hazel.join: An outing! Shop's locked, Ledger's in charge, and I've brought a fresh page for counting things. Lead on, {name}!
cheer: Ooh! That's one for the ledger. Top line, underlined twice.
I've sold that seed a thousand times. Never once seen it behave that nicely!
Lovely! That's three wins today. Four, if I count the biscuit I found.
Wait till the shop hears about this. Well, wait till I tell them. Which is tonight.
oops: Oh dear. I'll file that under 'Nearly'. It's a very thick file. Very friendly, too.
Not to worry! Most seeds take two tries. Some take nine. I've counted.
Hmm. Let's not count that one. I'm the counter, so I'm allowed to decide.
Ledger does that all the time. Then he sits on it and pretends he meant to.
hazel.win: What a day! I've counted everything twice and it all came out lovely. Same time next week?

tobin.join: Hm. Going out, are we? I'll bring the worms. You bring the quiet.
cheer: Hm. Good.
Nell would've clapped. I'll nod. Same thing.
That's the one. Knew it. Fish knew it too.
Caught one like that once. Bigger. Still. Good.
oops: Happens. River keeps a few for herself.
Fish said no. Fish are allowed.
Lost a pike that way once. Pike's still out there. Wearing my lure.
Breathe. Try again. River's not going anywhere. Mostly.
tobin.win: Good day. Not a tall tale, that one. Doesn't need to be.

mira.join: Packed a hammer, a spare hammer and a sandwich. Two of those are for emergencies. Let's go, {name}.
cheer: Clean work. I'd sign that.
See? Hit it where it wants to be hit. Grandad's rule.
Huh. That's better than I'd have done. Don't tell anyone I said that.
Solid. Like a good anvil. Highest praise I've got.
oops: Well, now we know one way that doesn't work. That's science.
Happens to me daily. Usually before breakfast.
That's not broken. That's just pre-fixed.
Lost a screw, found a lesson. Net gain, technically.
mira.win: Not bad. Not bad at all. Next time I'm bringing two sandwiches.

clem.join: I've packed scones, a flask and a rolling pin. Don't ask about the rolling pin. Off we go, pet.
cheer: There! Gentle hands. Wren's got them too. Must run in the family.
Lovely, dear. That's how my mother did it, and she'd have said so loudly.
Patience, a pinch of salt and a firm hand. Works on dough. Works on most people.
Oh, well done, pet. Have a scone. I'm not asking.
oops: Never mind, dear. The first pancake's always a mess. So's the second, sometimes.
Ha! Wren once did exactly that and blamed a goose. There was no goose.
Hush now. My knees say you'll get it next time. They're right about half the time.
It's only flour and pride, pet. Both brush off.
clem.win: A good day's work. Come home with me and we'll eat until we're sensible again.

pip.join: AN EXPEDITION! Sir Hopsalot's in one pocket and my map's in the other. Let's GO, {name}!
cheer: WHOA! That's going on the map! With a STAR!
Sir Hopsalot saw that! He's doing his proud croak!
That's the best thing I've seen since the snail with the stripe!
You're SO good at this. I'm writing 'EXPERT' next to your stick person.
oops: That's okay! Explorers fall over loads. It's in the rules. I wrote the rules.
Sir Hopsalot says that didn't count. He's a knight, so it's official.
I'm drawing that bit as 'HERE BE OOPS'. It's a real map thing. Probably.
Don't worry! I tripped on that exact root yesterday. And the day before.
pip.win: Best. Expedition. EVER. I'm drawing all of it tonight, even the boring bits!

rook.join: Hm. The sea can watch itself for a day. I'll walk with you, {name}. Mind the wind.
cheer: There. The tide's on your side today.
Well done. That one's going in the log.
Like a ship rounding the Point in fog. Steady, steady, then home.
The gulls saw that. They'll be insufferable about it for weeks.
oops: The sea takes. The sea gives back. Usually on a Tuesday.
No shame in it. Every captain runs aground once. I did it twice. Same rock.
Write it in the log as weather. Weather's nobody's fault.
Steady. One bad wave doesn't make a storm.
rook.win: A fair day, and a fair wind home. I'll log it as one of the good ones.

ingrid.join: Mm. I'll come. Bring a scarf. Wind always finds whoever forgot one.
cheer: Mm. Good.
Nicely done. Quiet hands.
There. You listened. That's most of it.
Old Mags couldn't have done better. That's a compliment. She's a very good sheep.
oops: Mm. Happens.
Stand still a moment. Then try again. It'll keep.
Wind took that one. Wind takes plenty. Gives some back.
Stubborn did the same once. She's still proud of it.
ingrid.win: Good day. Better company. ...Don't tell anyone I said that.

wren.join: Fine, I'll come. Someone has to stop you stepping on anything interesting, {name}.
cheer: Not bad. I'd have done it faster, but I've had a seventy-year head start.
See? It leaned toward you. They do that, when you listen.
Good. Now do it again without looking so surprised.
That's the Bramble touch. Took me years. Took you an afternoon. Rude.
oops: Hm. The plant won that round. Plants usually do.
Don't sulk. I once planted a whole bed of onions upside down. They forgave me.
That's step one: getting it wrong. Step two takes about forty years.
Clementine would say 'never mind, pet'. I'll say: again. Properly.
wren.win: Not a bad day. Don't tell Clementine I enjoyed it. She'll bake me a cake about it.

greet: Welcome to the Lantern & Ladle, {name}! Sit anywhere. Not there, that stool wobbles. It's had a long life.
Ah, {name}! Today's soup is a daring expedition into parsnip country. Few return. All are delighted.
I once crossed the Glimmer Fens with nothing but a spoon. These days I mostly stir with it.
Fresh notices on the board! Quests for the brave, the curious and the slightly bored.
Twenty years on the road and I never met a mountain I couldn't climb. Then I met a really good stew.
Hang up your hat and tell me everything. Strange tracks? Odd weather? Big mushrooms? I live for it.
Every bowl's an adventure, {name}. Today's is called 'The Leek Who Went Too Far'. It has dumplings.
Behold! A hero returns! Or a farmer. From back here it's hard to tell. Either way, there's bread.
rumors: A traveler swears a fox in the Mossy Woods stole one sock. Just the one. Keep an eye on your laundry.
Little lights over Lily Pond at dusk, I hear. Fireflies, probably. Probably.
Otters on the riverbanks, they say, sliding down the mud for the sheer joy of it. Fine role models.
Old miners left a crust for the bats, for luck. Said it kept the tunnels friendly. Can't hurt.
The gulls on the coast are up to something. Sharing secrets or stealing sandwiches. With gulls it's both.
Sheep bells on the wind some evenings, from way up high. Somebody's keeping a flock up there.
Someone still keeps watch out on the Point, they say. Lonely work. A visitor wouldn't go amiss.
Pip swears the Old Quarry talks back. Pip also swears Sir Hopsalot can read. Worth checking one of them.
Hazel counted the same shelf three times this morning. When Hazel recounts, something's running short.
Mira's been muttering at her anvil. She'll never ask for help. Which is exactly when to offer.
Gran's baking more than the whole valley can eat. Means she's happy, or she's thinking. Worth a visit either way.
Ask Tobin what's wrong and he'll say 'nothing'. Ask twice and you'll get a story. Ask three times and you'll get a fish.

farming: The turnip practically leaps into your hand.
Every seed sprouts at once, like a tiny round of applause.
The soil crumbles just right. Somewhere below, a worm nods approvingly.
The vine untangles itself and hands you its very best fruit.
The scarecrow would tip its hat, if it could. It very nearly manages.
fishing: A fish leaps straight into your bucket, then looks around as if it meant to all along.
Your line sings. The water holds its breath. Then: the catch of the week.
A perfect cast. Even the heron stops to watch.
The float dips once, politely, like a fish knocking before it comes in.
It's the sort of catch that becomes a tall tale. Except you've got the fish to prove it.
foraging: You part the ferns and there it is, as if it had been waiting for you.
A whole patch of the good stuff, right where nobody else thought to look.
A squirrel drops exactly what you were after and scampers off looking pleased with itself.
Your nose, your eyes and your luck all agree at once. Rare. Wonderful.
The path seems to bend just to show you something lovely.
mining: One tap and the rock splits clean, like a loaf fresh from Gran's oven.
The vein glitters in your lantern light, bright as a wink.
Your pick finds the sweet spot. The whole tunnel hums a happy little note.
A pebble rolls aside to reveal a gleam. The mountain was saving it for you.
Not a speck of dust out of place. Old miners would tip their helmets for that swing.
crafting: Every piece clicks together on the first try. It even looks better than the drawing.
The knot practically ties itself. Well, you tied it. But beautifully.
Not a single bent nail. Mira would frame it.
You stand back and admire it. It's sturdy enough to hold a whole committee meeting.
The grain lines up, the joints sit snug, and the whole thing hums with good work.
cooking: The kitchen fills with a smell so good the neighbors suddenly need to borrow sugar.
It rises perfectly. You didn't even peek. Gran would be proud.
One taste and your knees go a little wobbly. In the good way.
Golden on top, soft in the middle, and not a crumb out of place.
You season it without measuring and it's exactly right. Instinct, or magic. Possibly both.

farming: You plant the seed upside down. It will sort itself out. Eventually. Grumpily.
You water the scarecrow's boots instead of the beds. It seems grateful, at least.
A crow watches you dig the wrong row and makes a noise that sounds a lot like laughing.
You pull up a weed with great confidence. It was a carrot. The carrot forgives you.
Your boot sticks in the mud. You get free. The mud keeps the boot. Somewhere, Tobin senses an opportunity.
fishing: You slip into the creek. The heron looks embarrassed for you.
You reel in with great drama and land a very surprised clump of weed.
Your hook catches your own hat. Well. You caught something.
The fish takes the bait, looks you in the eye, and leaves. Rude, but impressive.
You cast beautifully, straight into a tree. The tree is not hungry.
foraging: You proudly pick a mushroom. It's a pinecone. With ambitions.
You reach for the berries. A squirrel reaches first and gives you a look.
You trip on a root, roll gently down a bank, and land in a very comfy patch of clover.
You sneeze at exactly the wrong moment. Every bird nearby files a complaint.
You follow a promising trail for ten minutes. It's your own footprints.
mining: Your pick bounces off the rock with a cheerful 'boing'. The rock wins this round.
You dig with great enthusiasm and uncover the other side of the same rock.
Your lantern flickers and you politely apologize to a stalagmite.
A puff of dust turns you an elegant shade of grey. Very distinguished.
You spot a glittering gem! It's your lantern's reflection. Still, lovely lantern.
crafting: You glue it together beautifully. Upside down. It's modern art now.
The knot you tie is magnificent and holds nothing at all.
You measure twice, cut once, and still end up with a very short plank.
Your creation wobbles, sighs, and lies down. It needs a rest. So do you.
You nail it firmly in place. Along with your sleeve. You and the shelf are close friends now.
cooking: You reach for the sugar and grab the salt. Bold choice. Brave, even.
The bread rises, looks around, and thinks better of it.
The pot boils over the moment you turn your back. It was waiting for that.
Your pancake flips beautifully and lands on top of the cupboard. It lives there now.
It smells wonderful, looks alarming, and tastes like an apology. Next time!
